metric.why: Rates rising after a decade of decline is the clearest market evidence that demand outran supply. Rate data is compiled by commercial research firms listed in the directory below; it is not republished here.
metric.definition: Market rate per kilowatt per month for leased capacity, the price signal for scarcity in each metro.

reading.body:
Rising colocation rental rates after a decade of decline are the clearest market signal that AI compute demand has outpaced available data center supply.

For ten years, as hyperscalers built capacity faster than demand grew, rates compressed downward. The reversal means operators can no longer keep pace. When the price of leased kilowatt-hours climbs in a competitive market, it reflects genuine scarcity, not arbitrary pricing. This matters for AI because training and inference clusters require not just electricity but physical space in buildings near power sources and network hubs. The constraint shifts from "can we build chips" to "can we build the facilities to plug them in."

Rate data is compiled by commercial research firms and reflects actual transactions in metro markets. The metric does not capture whether supply is constrained by power availability, grid connection limits, land, construction labor, or permitting delays. It measures only that something in the supply chain is tightening. This data sits alongside capital expenditure and equipment lead times, which together show whether the shortage stems from delayed building, delayed equipment, or both.
